acceptanceEvidence.1 bash refusal, every form, any pipeline: Real surface: branch run items 3 (plain `-R … undo`), 4 (`cd -- … && … op restore @-`, the && chain) and 5 (`abandon`) refused with isError=true; each reason names the invocation (`jj -R $LEGION_WORKSPACE undo`, `… op restore @-`, `… abandon`), says `every Legion issue workspace shares`, and gives the recovery (`new commit or \`jj restore <paths>\``, `send the owning architect the … log evidence`); no grant minted for any of the three. Negative control: the same three RAN on 1.22.2 and each left an operation in the log. Regression lock: legion.test.ts 'refuses a phase worker's bash command that would rewrite the shared jj operation log' (19 rows) — green in the 171.
acceptanceEvidence.2 jj restore <paths>, jj op log, jj op s: Real surface: branch run items 1 and 9 (`op log -n 3` / `-n 5`), item 2 (`describe -m "rig: marker before the guard checks"`, a quoted message) and item 8 (`restore --help | head -1`, the file-level restore subcommand in a pipeline) ran and each minted one grant; the subagent run's `op log` calls ran too. `jj op show` and a quoted `-m "undo this"` are covered by the regression lock only: legion.test.ts 'leaves file-level jj restore, jj op log, jj op show, and quoted message words alone' (13 rows, one mint each).
acceptanceEvidence.3 root architect and controller unaffect: Regression lock only — the grant rig boots one role (implementer) and has no root-architect or controller leg: legion.test.ts 'does not block bash calls from the controller session' (jj -R … undo -> undefined), 'blocks code tools in a root architect session' (jj undo -> the architect reason, never the shared-log one), 'applies the operation-log guard to every phase-worker role and leaves each role's sanctioned jj commands alone' (six roles; the reviewer's `.legion/` cleanup row allowed), plus the pre-existing 'restricts phase-worker tool access per LEGION_ROLE' and 'allows xd:// tool-device writes' — all green in the 171. The real-surface implementer run confirms the phase-worker branch of the same hook is what the production plugin tree loads (one legion.js instance from the profile's plugins/).
acceptanceEvidence.4 SKILL.md says blocked by the extension: Diff of skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md in commit 5c163ecc3169fb80e7f1d64ac8aaf6468e815085 (on the PR): the 'Shared operation safety' paragraph says the extension refuses the commands (bash, eval, hub, task subagents), names the recovery rule (new commit or jj restore <paths>; otherwise the architect with the log evidence) and tells workers to write mentioning text with the write tool. Reviewer verifies from the diff; this phase read the committed file.
acceptanceEvidence.5 eval code and hub start refused with t: Real surface: branch run item 6 (`eval` py subprocess argv `["jj","-R",…,"undo"]`) refused as `eval: jj undo` and item 7 (`hub` op start, application `jj`, args `-R /tmp/l45rig/ws undo`) refused as `hub: jj undo`, both isError=true with the identical shared-log/recovery text. Negative control: on 1.22.2 the hub start RAN (the supervised process performed undo 3ac039d0c094) and the eval reached the Python kernel (KeyError there, not a refusal). Regression lock: 'refuses eval code and hub input that mention jj with an operation-log rewrite, by the plain-text rule' (6 refused / 5 allowed).
acceptanceEvidence.6 a task subagent of a phase worker is r: Real surface: run l45-branch-subagent — the worker's `task` subagent JjUndoProbe ran (a) `op log -n 3` (ran), (b) `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" undo` (refused, isError=true, shared-log reason, in its own transcript and quoted verbatim in the parent's hub-wait result), (c) `echo subagent-still-runs && printenv LEGION_ROLE` (ran: `subagent-still-runs` / `implementer`); the subagent's bash calls minted no grant and called no daemon route (one mint in standin.log, the parent's); the OMP log shows the subagent's own extension instance 0e1c8610 handling its hooks. Op log head unchanged at 3640f172f102 afterwards. Regression lock: 'refuses a subagent's operation-log rewrite in a phase-worker pane while its other calls stay ungated'.
acceptanceEvidence.Errors: unparseable command -> plain-tex: Regression lock only (the nine-item prompt has no unterminated-quote row): step-1 row `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" describe -m 'undo` refused naming the trimmed command.

observations: Grant minting is itself evidence: on the branch plugin the stand-in logged 5 mints for 8 bash calls (the 3 refused bash calls minted none); on 1.22.2 it logged 8 for 8. The 'refused before any grant is minted' property therefore holds on the real surface, not only in the unit test.

The model added one bash call outside the prompt in both nine-item runs — `printenv LEGION_WORKSPACE`, resolving the prompt's placeholder for item 7's hub args — and, on the released run, a `read skill://using-jj` lookup. Neither is a rewrite; both ran. The extra calls explain the rig table's '8 bash calls' against the prompt's 7 bash items.

Under 1.22.2, item 6's eval failed with KeyError: 'LEGION_WORKSPACE' rather than performing an undo: OMP's eval Python kernel does not expose the pane's LEGION_WORKSPACE variable. Under the branch plugin the same call never reached the kernel (refused by the extension), which is the property under test; the kernel's environment is an OMP behaviour outside this issue and is noted, not worked around.

The grant rig's A–G table is not this run's evidence (README, `--prompt-file` paragraph): with a custom prompt it scores whatever bash calls the prompt caused (no record-grant or legion probes), so its FAIL rows for B, C, D, G are expected and meaningless here.

legion.yaml's trailing comment on omp_invocation says 'profile plugin stays 1.17.0'; the installed plugin in ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins is 1.22.2 (package.json and the byte-identical dist used for the negative control). The comment is stale; the negative control used what the panes actually load.

Deployment note carried from the plan: the guard reaches live panes only once the pi-envoy release built from this branch is installed into the legion profile before the daemon restarts. The tester's own pane runs 1.22.2, so this phase could type `jj … undo` in bash; the PR body and this handoff were nevertheless written through the write tool (and `legion handoff write` read its data from a file on stdin) so the same steps stay typeable after the release.
